original_article.research:
[Lähde: TechCrunch]
As its traffic continues to climb, alternative search engine DuckDuckGo is leaning into anti-AI sentiment with the launch of new browser extensions that allow users to set its no-AI search experience, noai.duckduckgo.com, as their default search engine.

Once enabled, users will be directed to the company’DuckDuckGo’s AI-free search page, where there are no AI-assisted answers, no chat prompts, and fewer AI images in the search results, the company claims. The extensions are currently available for Chrome and Firefox users. Meanwhile, people who have switched to the DuckDuckGo web browser already have their AI settings preserved, even if they clear their browser history.

---

[Lähde: MacRumors]
Privacy-focused search engine DuckDuckGo has seen a surge in demand for its "No AI" search option in the wake of Google's May 19th I/O announcements. Google debuted a new "intelligent" search box reimagined with AI. It features AI suggestions as an upgrade to autocomplete, support for follow-up questions, expanded Personal Intelligence for connecting Gmail and Google Photos, and Search agents.

DuckDuckGo told MacRumors that visits to its No AI search page more than tripled after Google's announcement. Traffic hit the 3x mark on May 28th, and has continued to climb. Visits have averaged around 84 percent above baseline consistently since May 19.

DuckDuckGo is embracing demand for No AI search options, and it is promoting new extensions available for Chrome and Firefox that set No AI search as the default.

No AI search has no AI-assisted answers, no chat interface, and it surfaces fewer AI images. DuckDuckGo can be set as the default search engine on Apple devices, but not the specific No AI page. DuckDuckGo has its own AI tools, but they are turned off for people who opt for the No AI experience.

DuckDuckGo plans to add No AI search settings to its original extensions for Chrome, Firefox, Edge, and Opera in the near future.

Along with DuckDuckGo, there are other privacy-focused search engine options that minimize AI results. Paid search engine Kagi is one example, with no visible AI information unless you opt for AI tools. Kagi is $5 per month for a limited number of searches, and $10 a month for unlimited searches.

Because it is a paid search engine, it does not have ads and it does not collect and sell user data.

---

[Lähde: PhoneWorld]
As artificial intelligence becomes a bigger part of online search, not everyone is embracing the change. Many users are now looking for search experiences that focus on traditional web results rather than AI-generated answers. This trend has helped DuckDuckGo’s “No AI” search option gain significant attention in recent weeks.

The increase in interest came shortly after Google’s latest announcements at its annual I/O event. Google introduced several new AI-powered search features designed to make searching more interactive and personalized. These updates include AI-generated suggestions, follow-up questions, intelligent search assistance, and tools that connect information from services such as Gmail and Google Photos.

While many users may appreciate these new capabilities, others appear to prefer a simpler search experience. According to reports, traffic to DuckDuckGo’s “No AI” search page more than tripled following Google’s announcement. The privacy-focused search engine has seen a steady increase in visitors who want search results without AI-generated content.

DuckDuckGo’s “No AI” mode is designed for users who want a more traditional search experience. The feature removes AI-generated answers, avoids chatbot-style interactions, and reduces the number of AI-created images shown in search results. Instead, users receive standard web results that allow them to explore information directly from websites.

The growing popularity of this option highlights an interesting divide among internet users. While AI tools can save time by summarizing information and answering questions directly, some people worry that AI-generated responses may not always provide complete or accurate information. Others simply prefer to browse websites themselves rather than relying on AI summaries.

Privacy is another factor driving interest in alternative search engines. DuckDuckGo has built its reputation on protecting user data and limiting online tracking. Unlike many major technology companies, the platform focuses on keeping searches private and does not create detailed profiles of its users. This approach continues to attract people who value online privacy.

To meet the increasing demand, DuckDuckGo is promoting browser extensions for Chrome and Firefox that allow users to make “No AI” search their default experience. The company also plans to expand these settings to additional browser extensions in the future, making the feature easier to access.

[Lähde: Lifehacker]
It's no secret that Google, like most big tech companies, has gone all-in on AI. The company believes it is the future, and, as such, has injected the technology into every one of its products, none more visibly than Google Search. Over the past two years, Google has introduced AI summaries that seek to answer your questions, pulling the information from websites that fewer and fewer users are actually visiting and reading for themselves.

Given this trend, it should hardly come as a surprise that during I/O 2026, Google announced "a new era for AI Search." This "era" essentially marks an expansion of its investment in AI in Search: In addition to rolling out its new Gemini 3.5 Flash model to Search, Google is making it even easier to use its AI-generated results (or, perhaps, harder to avoid them). You can now expand an AI Overview to continue the conversation in AI Mode, and keep receiving answers without engaging with any primary sources yourself. Google will also soon offer select users access to Search "agents," which can take actions on your behalf on the web.

payload.title: DuckDuckGo helpottaa tekoälyttömän haun käyttöönottoa Chromessa ja Firefoxissa
payload.summary: DuckDuckGo tuo Chrome- ja Firefox-käyttäjille selainlaajennukset, joilla yhtiön tekoälyvastauksista vapaa No AI -hakukokemus voidaan asettaa oletushauksi. Kysyntä on kasvanut Googlen toukokuisten hakujulkistusten jälkeen.
payload.content:
DuckDuckGo on alkanut tarjota Chrome- ja Firefox-selaimille laajennuksia, joiden avulla käyttäjät voivat asettaa yhtiön No AI -hakusivun oletushauksi. Yhtiön mukaan noai.duckduckgo.com-sivulla ei näytetä tekoälyn tuottamia vastauksia eikä chat-kehotteita, ja hakutuloksissa on vähemmän tekoälykuvia.

## Tekoälytön haku oletukseksi

Uudet selainlaajennukset on suunnattu käyttäjille, jotka haluavat tehdä DuckDuckGon tekoälyttömästä hausta pysyvän oletuskokemuksen omassa selaimessaan. Kun laajennus on otettu käyttöön, selaimen haut ohjautuvat DuckDuckGon No AI -hakusivulle.

Kyse ei lähdeaineiston perusteella ole kokonaan uudesta hakukoneesta, vaan helpommasta tavasta käyttää yhtiön erillistä tekoälyvapaaksi kuvattua hakusivua. Laajennukset ovat tällä hetkellä saatavilla Chromelle ja Firefoxille.

DuckDuckGon oman selaimen käyttäjillä tekoälyasetukset säilyvät jo valmiiksi myös silloin, kun selainhistoria tyhjennetään. Chrome- ja Firefox-laajennukset tuovat saman valinnan näkyvämmin käyttäjille, jotka eivät ole vaihtaneet DuckDuckGon omaan selaimeen.

## Kysyntä kasvoi Googlen julkistusten jälkeen

DuckDuckGon mukaan kiinnostus No AI -hakua kohtaan kasvoi Googlen 19. toukokuuta pitämien I/O-julkistusten jälkeen. Google esitteli tuolloin tekoälyllä uudistettua hakukenttää, tekoälyehdotuksia automaattisen täydennyksen laajennuksena, jatkokysymyksiä tukevia toimintoja, Gmailiin ja Google Kuviin kytkeytyvää henkilökohtaisempaa älykkyyttä sekä hakua käyttäviä agentteja.

DuckDuckGo kertoi, että käynnit sen No AI -hakusivulla yli kolminkertaistuivat Googlen julkistuksen jälkeen. Kolminkertainen taso saavutettiin 28. toukokuuta, ja liikenteen kerrotaan jatkaneen kasvuaan sen jälkeen.

No AI -sivun käynnit ovat olleet 19. toukokuuta lähtien keskimäärin noin 84 prosenttia aiempaa perustasoa korkeammalla. DuckDuckGo vastaa kasvuun tuomalla esiin laajennuksia, joilla No AI -haku voidaan asettaa oletukseksi.

## Saatavuus laajenee myöhemmin

DuckDuckGo aikoo laajentaa näitä asetuksia myöhemmin myös muihin selainlaajennuksiin, jotta tekoälyttömän haun käyttöönotto olisi helpommin saatavilla. Tarkempaa aikataulua tai seuraavia selaimia ei lähdeaineistossa kerrottu.
summary_bullets: DuckDuckGo julkaisi Chrome- ja Firefox-laajennukset No AI -haun asettamiseksi oletukseksi.
No AI -hakusivulla ei yhtiön mukaan ole tekoälyvastauksia tai chat-kehotteita.
Kävijämäärät kasvoivat Googlen 19. toukokuuta esittelemien tekoälyhakutoimintojen jälkeen.
